Unit 1

The pirates and the parrot
1 Look, listen and point.

2 Read and write the names.

1. He’s got long hair. It’s curly and blonde. He’s got a moustache and he’s quite short. He is very fat.
His name is Jack.

2. This pirate is very short. He’s got a long black beard, but he hasn’t got any hair! He’s wearing a blue coat.
His name is ______.

3. He’s got long, curly hair and he is tall. His hair isn’t blonde. He’s wearing a red scarf round his neck.
His name is ______.

4. He’s got long, straight hair. He’s very thin and he’s quite tall. He’s got a parrot on his shoulder. He’s wearing a blue scarf round his neck.
His name is ______.

Now go to Workbook page 7

3 Listen and draw lines.

We’re having a pirate party! What do you want to wear?

4 Look, point and say.

He’s got black hair and a black beard.

Number 1.

5 Talk about these people.

1. You.

2. Your friend.

3. A man in your family.

4. A woman in your family.

I’m quite tall. I’ve got short, brown hair.

I have got / He has gotquite/verycurly / long / blackhair.
I am / She isquite/verytall / short.

Now go to Workbook page 9

6 Look at the picture. Read and write Yes or No.

1. The pirate with the black coat has got a parrot on his shoulder. No

2. The pirate with the curly, blonde hair is drinking lemonade. ______

3. The pirate with the black beard is sitting in the tree. ______

4. The pirate with the black moustache is carrying a box of treasure. ______

5. The pirate with the red scarf is looking at the treasure. ______

7 Ask and answer. Use the words in the box to help you.

boat watermelon bag hat

lemonade ice cream kite ball

Who has got a ball?

The boy with short, curly, black hair.

The boy with the curly hair has got a parrot.

The pirates with the black hats are sitting on the beach.

Now go to Workbook page 11

It’s our world!

1 Look at the photos. Do you think these boys are brothers? Why?

2 Read the text. Answer the questions.

Hi, my name’s Bruno. My brother is Bernardo. We’re from Brazil. We are nine years old and we’re twins. This means we have the same mother and father, we were born on the same day, and we’re the same age. We have got dark brown hair and dark brown eyes. My hair is quite short and Bernardo’s is quite long. We are tall, but you can’t see that in this photo! I think I am very different from Bernardo, but people often think I am him!

2 1. Which photo is of Bruno and his brother?

2. Which boy is Bruno?

3 Look again at the photos on page 12. Read the sentences and write 1, 2 or 3.

1. They have got blonde hair. ______

2. The two brothers have got very short hair. ______

3. One brother has got quite short hair and one brother has got quite long hair. ______

4. They have got blue eyes. ______

4 Read what Bruno says about twins and circle Yes or No.

My brother and I are ‘identical twins’. Identical twins look like each other. Identical twins are always two girls or two boys. Some of my friends are twins, but they aren’t identical.

1. Bruno is an identical twin. Yes / No

2. Identical twins don’t look like each other. Yes / No

3. Identical twins are always two boys or two girls Yes / No

4. Some of Bruno’s friends are identical twins. Yes / No

5 Talk to a friend. Then tell the class.

1. Do you know any twins?

2. What do you think is not good about being a twin?

Now go to Workbook pages 12–13

Unit 2

My friends, the animals

Useful Language

always

never

often

sometimes
1 Look, listen and point.

Do you know and can you say
a lot of animal names today?
An elephant, a horse, a hippo and a bat.
A kangaroo, a cow, a goat and a cat.
A crocodile, a bear, a mouse and a dog.
A lion, a tiger, a giraffe and a frog.
Now we know and we can say
a lot of animal names today.

2 Listen and sing.

3 Say sentences with always, often, sometimes or never.

Max always eats bananas.
4 Listen and draw lines.

I always give water to my pet.

You sometimes play with animals.

Sue often paints pictures of animals.

We never leave a pet in a hot car.

Now go to Workbook page 15

Useful Language

after

at home

before

careful

leave

look after

5 Read the sentences about pets. Write the letter of each picture next to the correct sentence.

Look after your pets, please.

1. Always say nice things to your pet. G

2. Never give a lot of cake to a pet bird. ______

3. Always take your dog to play on the grass in the park. ______

4. Always be careful of pets with big teeth. ______

5. Never leave the door of a bird cage open. ______

6. Always take your dog for a walk. ______

7. Always give your pet a lot of water. ______

8. Never leave your pet in a hot car. ______

6 Listen and read about Bill and his pets. Tick (✓) or cross (✗).

When I get up in the morning, I always go and see my pets. Sally, Rover and Clover are always awake. I say ‘Hello’ to them but I never play with them before school.

After school, I often play with my pet bird, Sally. Sally sometimes flies to me and sits on my shoulder.

In the afternoon, I always take Rover and Clover for a walk in the park. Rover and Clover like running on the grass.

At night, Sally always sleeps in my house. Rover and Clover never sleep in the house. They always sleep in the garden.

1. Rover and Clover are always awake when Bill gets up. ✓

2. Bill plays with Rover and Clover before school. ☐

3. Bill often plays with his pet bird after school. ☐

4. Bill always takes Rover and Clover for a walk. ☐

5. Bill, Rover and Clover always go to the park. ☐

6. Rover and Clover never sleep in Bill’s room. ☐

Now go to Workbook page 17

7 Read the sentences. Do you do these things? Write always, often, sometimes or never.

1. Look after a pet. ______

2. Give water to animals. ______

3. Take a pet for a walk. ______

4. Wash a pet. ______

5. Play with a pet. ______

6. Clean a bird cage. ______

7. Draw pictures of animals. ______

8. Watch animals on TV. ______

9. Give food to birds. ______

10. Take photos of an animal. ______

8 Talk about animals, pets and you. Use always, often, sometimes or never.

I always look after my pets.

9 Ask and answer.

Do you draw pictures of animals?

Yes, I sometimes draw pictures of animals. What about you?

Now go to Workbook page 19

1 Look at the photos. Guess the answers to the questions before you read the text.

1. How old is the girl?

2. Where is the girl from?

3. Who is the man with her?

4. What is the man’s job?

2 Now read and answer the questions in exercise 1.
Hello. My name is Preet, and I’m from India. I am eight years old. This is my dad. His name is Arun. He is a guide at Ranthambore Park. Tigers live there.

3 Read and circle Yes or No.

Tigers are in danger. There are not many tigers in the world now. People come to Ranthambore Park in India to see them. Dad drives visitors to the park and helps them to find tigers. In the park, they can watch tigers and take photos of them. Dad tells them about the tigers. He thinks we all need to look after our world.

1. Are tigers in danger? Yes / No

2. Are there a lot of tigers in the world? Yes / No

3. Do people come to Ranthambore to see tigers? Yes / No

4. Does Arun drive tigers to the park? Yes / No

5. Can people take pictures of tigers in Ranthambore Park? Yes / No

4 Talk to a friend. Choose two animals that you like. Answer the questions.

1. Where do your animals live?

2. Are your animals in danger?

3. Which animals are in danger in your country?

5 Now tell the class about your animals.

Now go to Workbook pages 20–21

Unit 4

The weather’s very nice
1 Look, listen and point.
2 Listen and write the numbers.
3 Listen, read and draw lines. Then sing the song.

The weather’s very hot today.
The sky is blue. What can we do?
It’s sunny and it’s hot today.
We want to play this morning.

The weather’s very cold today.
Look at the ice. It’s very nice.
It’s snowing and it’s cold today.
We want to play this morning.

The weather’s very wet today.
The sky is grey. Can we play?
It’s raining and it’s wet today.
We want to play this morning.

The wind is very strong today.
There’s a cloudy sky. Can we fly?
It’s a windy, cold and cloudy day.
We want to play this morning.

Now go to Workbook page 31

Useful Language

bad difference different

4 Listen and read.

Bill is reading an email about a friend’s holiday.

ToBill
FromJim

Hi Bill,

I’m on holiday in a small house in a big jungle. It is very different from home. There are differences in the weather and the plants and the animals.

The weather is very hot. In the morning there are no clouds and we can see the sun. Sometimes the weather is bad in the afternoons. It rains and is very wet.

I can see mountains from my window. There is a river next to the house. I sometimes go for a swim there. I often see monkeys and birds in the trees. It’s beautiful here.

Jim

5 Read and tick (✓) or cross (✗).

1. Jim’s on holiday in a big house. ✗

2. There aren’t any trees in the jungle. ☐

3. The weather is very hot. ☐

4. You can’t see the sun in the morning. ☐

5. The house is next to the river. ☐

6. Jim swims in the river. ☐

7. He can see birds in the jungle. ☐

8. He isn’t enjoying his holiday. ☐

Useful Language

a country everything a place

6 Listen and read.

May is reading an email from a girl in Canada.

ToMay
FromJane

Hello May,

My name is Jane and I am eight years old. I live with my mum and dad and my brother. He’s six. We live on an island in Canada. It’s a beautiful place. The weather here is very cold and windy and it often snows. There is snow and ice and everything is white and clean. The days are short and the nights are long.

The sea is very cold but there are a lot of fish. I sometimes see whales in the sea and sea birds in the sky. Is it hot in your country? Tell me about your home.

Jane

4. What does Jane sometimes see? ______

It’s our world!

1 Look at the photos. Guess the answers to the questions before you read the text.

1. How old is the girl?

2. Is she on holiday?

3. Is she in a hot or cold place?

My name is Sophia. I live in La Plata in Argentina and I am nine years old. I am on holiday with my family. I’m here with my sister Anna, my mum and my dad. We are on holiday on a ship. You can see the ship in the picture. We sleep in rooms called cabins on the ship. There is a cabin for my mum and dad, and a cabin for my sister and me. We are in Antarctica. There is lots of snow and ice here. It’s the coldest place in the world! You have to wear very warm clothes here.

2 Now read and answer the questions in exercise 1.

3 Read and circle the correct answer.

1. Sophia’s holiday is in a. the cabin. b. La Plata. c. Antarctica.

2. Anna is Sophia’s a. mum. b. sister. c. dad.

3. A cabin is a a. person. b. room. c. ship.

4 Read and circle the correct answer.

In the photo, you can see some emperor penguins. They are birds. They can live in very cold places with a lot of snow and ice. There are lots of emperor penguins in Antarctica. Emperor penguins can walk and swim, but they can’t fly. They fish in the cold sea. They have one baby a year.

1. Emperor penguins are fish / birds.

2. Emperor penguins can live in very hot / cold places.

3. There are lots of emperor penguins in Antarctica / the Arctic circle.

4. Emperor penguins can swim and walk / swim and fly.

5 Talk to a friend. Then tell the class.

1. Is the weather in your country hot or cold?

2. What is your favourite weather? What do you do when the weather is like that?
